analysis.title: Fox Corp. (FOXA): F1Q27 First Take: EBITDA beat on World Cup, political, and TV opex
key_insights: Goldman expects FOXA to trade higher on the F1Q27 revenue and EBITDA beat. The beat was broad-based across all segments but mainly came from Television advertising and operating expenses.

Adjusted EBITDA was $1.64 bn against GSe $1.41 bn and Visible Alpha consensus $1.34 bn. Adjusted EPS was $2.54 against GSe $2.10 and consensus $1.99. Revenue was $4.57 bn against GSe $4.40 bn and consensus $4.29 bn.
Television advertising revenue was $1.71 bn against GSe $1.65 bn and consensus $1.50 bn. Goldman names better-than-expected World Cup and political advertising as likely drivers of the beat.
Television adjusted EBITDA was $934 mn against GSe $746 mn and consensus $668 mn. The segment margin was 34.4% against 28.1% in GSe, and Goldman also credits lower TV operating expenses.
Cable Network Programming revenue was $1.80 bn against GSe $1.77 bn and consensus $1.74 bn. Segment adjusted EBITDA was $859 mn against GSe $820 mn and consensus $815 mn.

Distribution revenue beat in both segments: Cable Network $1.20 bn against GSe $1.17 bn and consensus $1.14 bn, Television $850 mn against GSe $841 mn and consensus $831 mn. Goldman reads these beats, together with the Corporate & Other beat, as momentum at Fox One.
Misses were small. Cable Network Other revenue of $230 mn was below consensus of $242 mn, and Television Other revenue of $155 mn was below both GSe and consensus of $165 mn and $168 mn.

Goldman is Not Rated on FOXA because it is acting as financial advisor in an announced strategic matter involving Fox Corporation. The rating, target price and estimates are removed under that policy, and the last published target was $81 on 11 May 2026.
FOXA traded at $63.24 on 30 Oct 2026 with a market cap of $30.0 bn and enterprise value of $31.3 bn.

market_movers.rationale: Goldman says FOX should trade higher on the revenue and EBITDA beat across all segments, led by Television advertising and opex. Distribution beats point to Fox One momentum.

earnings_insights: FOXA F1Q27 reported adjusted EBITDA $1.64 bn (+54% y/y) vs GSe $1.41 bn and Visible Alpha consensus $1.34 bn. These are estimates and the $1.64 bn is the printed figure.
FOXA F1Q27 reported adjusted diluted EPS $2.54 vs GSe $2.10 and consensus $1.99. The $2.54 is the printed adjusted figure and the other two are estimates.
FOXA F1Q27 reported revenue $4.57 bn (+22% y/y) vs GSe $4.40 bn and consensus $4.29 bn.

Television segment reported revenue $2.71 bn vs GSe $2.66 bn and consensus $2.49 bn. Advertising was $1.71 bn (+60% y/y) vs GSe $1.65 bn and consensus $1.50 bn, and segment adjusted EBITDA was $934 mn vs GSe $746 mn and consensus $668 mn.

Cable Network Programming reported revenue $1.80 bn vs GSe $1.77 bn and consensus $1.74 bn. Affiliate fee revenue was $1.20 bn vs GSe $1.17 bn and consensus $1.14 bn, and segment adjusted EBITDA was $859 mn vs GSe $820 mn and consensus $815 mn.

Goldman's own estimates for upcoming quarters, which carry the pre-print model: 9/26E EPS $2.10, 12/26E EPS $1.10, 3/27E EPS $1.27. Fiscal 6/27E EPS is $6.03 and EBITDA $4,243.9 mn. These predate the print.
